---
title: 'Introduction to agentic AI'
title-block-banner: false
---

A course for **teachers and researchers** on using coding agents (**Claude Code**
and **Codex**) to get real work done: cleaning data, making reproducible
figures, reviewing literature, extracting data from documents, building course
pages and interactive apps.

You do **not** need to know programming, the command line or GitHub. We teach
the parts you need, as you need them. The agent writes the code; you learn to
describe the task, check the result and keep your work organised.

## How the course works

- Work through the sidebar from top to bottom. Each unit has a **lecture**
  (slides) and an **exercise**.
- Every exercise has a **worked example** on shared data, and a part where you
  apply the same skill to **your own project**. You choose that project at the
  end of Part 1.
- Agents give different answers each time. Your session will not look exactly
  like the slides, and that is expected.

## Start here

1. [Why agentic AI?](why-agentic/lec.qmd)
2. [Accounts and installation](accounts-install/exercise.qmd): which
   subscriptions you need and how to install the tools.

## The parts of the course

- **Part 1: Getting started.** What an agent is, installing it, the terminal,
  your first delegations, how LLMs fail, and privacy. Ends with choosing your
  own project.
- **Part 2: A project that lasts.** Delegating well, organising a project folder
  for an agent, git as an undo button, reproducible figures.
- **Part 3: Sharing.** GitHub, a course or project page, interactive demos,
  Shiny apps.
- **Part 4: Literature, documents and the web.** Literature review, extracting
  data from PDFs, analysing grant results, preparing for grant reviewers.
- **Part 5: Scaling up.** Claude and Codex in parallel, custom skills, reading
  other people's code.
- **Tracks.** RNA-seq, simulation, image analysis in Python, survey data,
  teaching materials.
